label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

report.summary: Publications stalled for ~30 s while arrivals continued, then caught up in a burst. The stall coincided with refused connections to the consumer; DB, pool and API were healthy. A permanently FAILED backlog also exists.

findings.claim: Outbox publications stopped for about 20-30 s while arrivals stayed steady, then a catch-up burst followed; pending peaked at 92.
findings.reason: Per-bucket publications went 28,0,0,0,37,82 against constant 28 arrivals; pending was 78 at 19:29:08 and 2 by 19:30:18.

findings.claim: Delivery attempts hit CONNECTION_FAILED (428, sub-ms, no consumer record) alongside 421 successes, so the consumer endpoint was refusing connections during the stall.
findings.reason: Failures return in ~0.3 ms with no consumer record, which fits refused connections. The failure timestamps were not lined up against the stall buckets.

findings.claim: Transfer API, DB pool and DB locks were healthy, so the lateness is in the outbox-to-consumer hop, not transfer handling.
findings.reason: No 5xx, p99 0.25 s, 0 pool timeouts or pending borrowers, and 0 blocked sessions.

findings.claim: 296 outbox rows are permanently FAILED, with the oldest undelivered at about 6400 s. This is a separate, older backlog.
findings.reason: The failed count stayed at 296 and the oldest age grew linearly all window, so these rows are not being retried.

limitations: Only the earliest 100 of 849 attempt records are listed, so the failures are not time-aligned to the 0-publication buckets.
There is no consumer-side availability or process log explaining why connections were refused.
next_checks: List the CONNECTION_FAILED attempts by timestamp and compare them with the 19:28:40-19:29:10 stall.
Check the consumer at 127.0.0.1:18090 for restarts or listener downtime, and find why 296 rows are FAILED.

alternatives.reason: No poller-side logs cover the gap, though the retry attempts (attempt 3) suggest the poller kept running.
alternatives.hypothesis: Poller or publisher stall, not a consumer outage, caused the gap.

alternatives.reason: The pool never queued and no blocking was sampled.
alternatives.hypothesis: DB or pool contention delayed publication.
